title: World
description: A persistent fictional universe (a 'world bible') in which many stories take place. Captures everything professional studios put in a series bible plus the locked art-style guide that guarantees visual consistency across every illustration.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier, unique across the workspace. Becomes the first path segment on GitHub Pages (/world/...).

tagline.description: One memorable sentence that sells the world.

premise.description: 2-4 sentences: the central idea, what makes this world special, and the kind of stories it produces.

tone.description: Emotional register. Lean bold and fun, e.g. ['madcap','adventurous','mischievous','a-little-spooky'] or ['witty','high-stakes','laugh-out-loud']. Cozy/gentle is fine as ONE colour in the mix, not the whole palette.

target_years.description: Reader AGES (in years) this world is designed to serve, e.g. [5,6,7]. The primary audience knob. Individual stories pick one age (story.target_year).

target_age_bands.description: DEPRECATED — legacy coarse age bands, kept only so existing worlds stay valid. Use target_years instead; the scaffolder may still derive this for display.

languages.description: BCP-47 language codes the world supports.

rules.description: The laws of the world (how magic/technology/society works). Stories must never contradict these — they are the consistency contract. Each rule may be a plain string (the validator gives it a positional id r1, r2, …) or an object with a stable `id` + `text` so a story can reference it via `affirms_rules`.

id.description: Stable id a story's affirms_rules can point at.

timeline.description: Ordered eras or key events that ground continuity across stories.

motifs.description: Recurring visual/thematic motifs (objects, symbols, refrains) that make the world feel cohesive.

themes.description: Recurring ideas/flavours the world plays with (e.g. adventure, mischief, mystery, friendship) — NOT values or life-lessons to teach. These colour the fun, they don't moralise it.

tags.description: Library tags used for browsing/filtering on the published site.

ageBand.description: 0-3 board book, 3-5 pre-reader, 5-7 early reader (K-1), 7-9 (grade 2-3), 9-12 middle grade, grown-up (adult reader).

artStyle.description: The locked visual identity. Every illustration prompt is assembled from these fields so the whole world looks like one artist drew it.

palette.description: The world's master palette. Re-stated in every prompt to lock color.

influences.description: Stated artistic influences (illustrators/films) — used as style anchors, not for copying.

prompt_style_block.description: The exact phrase appended to EVERY image prompt in this world. This is the single most important consistency lever. e.g. 'soft watercolor children's book illustration, warm muted palette (#f4e1c1 cream, #6b8f71 sage, #d98a5b terracotta), gentle rim lighting, rounded shapes, hand-painted paper texture, cozy storybook mood'.

negative_prompt.description: What to avoid in every image (e.g. 'photorealism, harsh shadows, scary expressions, text artifacts, extra fingers').

aspect_ratio.description: Default page aspect ratio (full-bleed image pages).

text_treatment.description: How embedded page text sits on the full-page image so it stays legible.

placement.description: Default text position for pages that don't set layout.text_position. Same enum as the story schema's layout.text_position — the single source of truth for where text sits.

scrim.description: Legibility device, e.g. 'soft cream rounded panel at 85% opacity'.
